### recall: switched network 



![](/switches/texfig/switched-network-recall-switched-network.figure.svg){fig-alt="Diagram of a single network (represented by a cloud) implemented by several switches. Each computer is conencted to one of the switches, and two of the switches are each connectedto a third."}


### hubs and switches  {.smaller}

![](/switches/texfig/switched-network-hubs-and-switches.figure.svg)
 

* difference is hidden inside
* hub: electrically connects hosts --- as if shared wires
* switch: decides what to send on each output


### history: multi-access to switched


* a lot of early networking technology was multi-access
* wireless (wifi, cellular) and most home broadband still is 
<hr class="vspace" />
* most wired networks are <i>switched</i>  
   * frames mostly directed to correct machine
* often same frame format as multi-access
   * switching is "optimization" where hosts don't need to handle irrelevant frames

### switching versus routing  {.smaller}


* switches --- forward frames for common network
* routers --- forward packets between networks 
<hr class="vspace" />
* basically same functionality
* differences: 
   * extra layer for internetwork packets
   * (typically) more complex mechanism to decide where to forward
* will start with simpler switching
